items.readable_text:
Content:
The method of subtracting numbers in scientific notation with different powers of ten is similar to adding them. We follow the usual three steps:

Content:
- Step 1: Identify the smaller number.
- Step 2: Rewrite the smaller number to have the same power of ten as the larger number.
- Step 3: Subtract the two numbers as usual.

Content:
For instance, let's compute the following difference:

Content:
[MATH: \left(9 \times 10^{7} \right) - \left(8 \times 10^{6} \right)]

Content:
The second number is the smaller of the two, so we rewrite it to have the same power of [MATH: 10] as the first number, as follows:
[MATH: 8 × 10^{6}|=; 8 × 10^{7 − 1}|=; 8 × 10^{− 1 + 7}|=; 8 × 10^{− 1} × 10^{7}|=; 0.8 × 10^{7}]

Content:
Finally, we can carry out the subtraction as usual:
[MATH: (9 × 10^{7}) − (8 × 10^{6})|=; (9 × 10^{7}) − (0.8 × 10^{7})|=; (9 − 0.8) × 10^{7}|=; 8.2 × 10^{7}]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The method of subtracting numbers in scientific notation with different powers of ten is similar to adding them. We follow the usual three steps:

Content:
- Step 1: Identify the smaller number.
- Step 2: Rewrite the smaller number to have the same power of ten as the larger number.
- Step 3: Subtract the two numbers as usual.

Content:
For instance, let's compute the following difference:

Content:
[MATH: \left(9 \times 10^{7} \right) - \left(8 \times 10^{6} \right)]

Content:
The second number is the smaller of the two, so we rewrite it to have the same power of [MATH: 10] as the first number, as follows:
[MATH: 8 × 10^{6}|=; 8 × 10^{7 − 1}|=; 8 × 10^{− 1 + 7}|=; 8 × 10^{− 1} × 10^{7}|=; 0.8 × 10^{7}]

Content:
Finally, we can carry out the subtraction as usual:
[MATH: (9 × 10^{7}) − (8 × 10^{6})|=; (9 × 10^{7}) − (0.8 × 10^{7})|=; (9 − 0.8) × 10^{7}|=; 8.2 × 10^{7}]

---

Now, carrying out the subtraction, we get
[MATH: (6.2 × 10^{13}) − (8.1 × 10^{12})|=; (6.2 × 10^{13}) − (0.81 × 10^{13})|=; (6.2 − 0.81) × 10^{13}|=; 5.39 × 10^{13}.]
